name: DND Flyway (Delhi-Noida Direct)
officialName: Delhi Noida Direct Flyway (Delhi-NOIDA Bridge and Ashram Flyover)

concession.modelName: Concession with a guaranteed 20% annual return on the 'Total Cost of Project'
concession.operator: Noida Toll Bridge Company Ltd (NTBCL), incorporated 8 Apr 1996; sponsored by IL&FS
concession.grantingAuthority: New Okhla Industrial Development Authority (NOIDA), Government of Uttar Pradesh
concession.tollEndCondition: Tolls until the 'Total Cost of Project' (project cost + major maintenance + any shortfall in a 20% annual return) was recovered, for 30 years or until recovery, with two-year extensions (Article 14 and Annexure F). The Supreme Court held the formula unreasonable and against public policy.

projectCost.note: Original cost as on the Commissioning Date. CAG found it should have been ₹281.12 crore.

amount.note: Annual toll income for 2001-2016, per the CAG report quoted by the Supreme Court (para 86).
CAG: total income ₹1,103 crore against total expenses of ₹1,136.26 crore, which CAG said included pre-commissioning and unnecessary expenditure (paras 83-84).

timeline.title: MoU for a Delhi-Noida bridge
timeline.description: NOIDA, the Delhi Administration and IL&FS sign an MoU.

timeline.title: Concession Agreement signed
timeline.description: NOIDA and IL&FS (sponsors) and NTBCL (concessionaire). No competitive bidding was held (CAG). A 20% annual return was allowed when the prime lending rate was 13% (CAG).

timeline.title: Flyway opens
timeline.description: Opened for public use (the Commissioning Date). Original cost on that date: ₹325.99 crore.

timeline.title: Residents' associations file a PIL
timeline.description: The Federation of Noida Residents Welfare Associations files PIL No. 60214 of 2012 in the Allahabad High Court.

timeline.title: Allahabad High Court ends tolling
timeline.description: A Division Bench rules that NTBCL "shall not impose any user fee/toll from the commuters", holds Article 13 of the Concession Agreement "bad and inoperative", and severs Article 14. The flyway is toll-free from this date.

timeline.title: Supreme Court orders a CAG audit
timeline.description: On NTBCL's appeal (SLP(C) 33403/2016), the Supreme Court issues notice and directs the CAG to audit NTBCL's cost-recovery claims. CAG files its report in a sealed cover on 22 Mar 2017.

timeline.title: Supreme Court upholds toll-free DND
timeline.description: The appeal is dismissed. The court holds the contract 'unfair, unjust and inconsistent with Constitutional norms', NOIDA's delegation of toll powers invalid, and finds NTBCL has recovered its costs and profits. It says 'the public has been defrauded'. No refund is ordered.

timeline.title: Review petition dismissed
timeline.description: The Supreme Court dismisses NTBCL's review petition. It agrees to consider modifying its observations about director Pradeep Puri.

analysis.summary: The DND Flyway has been toll-free since 26 Oct 2016. The Supreme Court upheld this in Dec 2024, finding that NTBCL had already recovered its construction cost and a fair profit, and that the 20%-return formula was unreasonable and against public policy. CAG found toll income of ₹892.51 crore over 2001-2016 against an original cost of ₹325.99 crore.

reasonsStillTolled.text: Tolls ended because the courts found the concessionaire had recovered its costs and profit, and that the contract's open-ended 20%-return formula was unreasonable and contrary to public policy.
The 'Total Cost of Project' grew because unrecovered returns compounded at 20% a year, and items such as ₹11 crore in legal fees and ₹72.25 lakh in corporate gifts were added to it (CAG).

CAG concluded that only around Rs 15 crore remained to be recovered as of 31 Mar 2016, and that NTBCL had made profits for 11 years, paid Rs 243.07 crore in dividends and repaid its debt; the Supreme Court adopted these conclusions (paras 83, 86). NTBCL's counsel argued the CAG report showed at least Rs 30 crore still recoverable (para 5(h)).

openQuestions: What is the outcome of NTBCL's arbitration against NOIDA (SLP(C) 8060/2019, to be decided separately)?
Who maintains the flyway now, at whose cost, and until when?
Will NOIDA recover any of the excess collected, or the outdoor-advertising dues the court left to the lease dispute process?

sources.title: Noida Toll Bridge Company Ltd v. Federation of Noida Residents Welfare Association & Ors, 2024 INSC 1027 (SLP(C) 33403/2016)
sources.note: Full text read on Indian Kanoon; check against the signed judgment on sci.gov.in. CAG findings are quoted at paras 59-62 and 83-86.
